doc: Two joins share the source A. A join is listed under each source at the position of that source's transition into it, so A lists J2 before J1. J1 is offered by B and J2 by C (the last source of each in post-order); a join is taken only if it is the first enabled transition of every source.

steps.doc: A's first enabled transition is J2, so J1 is blocked although B offers it before C offers J2. Ignoring A's disagreement would take J1 (eX) instead.
J2's guard fails, so A's first enabled transition is J1. The actions of the transitions into J1 run in file order (B's before A's), then J1's own.
